trigger: a device already contained under exceptions E1 gets a second record with different exceptions E2 (the first record force-ended server-side) and the apply hits self_host or own_addresses_unreadable (transient, or permanent where AF_NETLINK is denied)
classification_rationale: the refusal returns before apply_and_verify, so the device never emits the allow_set_unchanged note and the server then confirms a record whose allow set the device is not enforcing, contradicting the documented rule that a refused apply never confirms
summary: A refused apply on an already-contained device let the server confirm a record whose allow set the device never applied (verified by running the real server decision functions); fixed in a638d28c27 by skipping the self-host check only when the device's own record is already active (shape (a)), with the server-side half filed as #8519 and the divergence from the accepted plan raised again as G8-3.

trigger: an allocation failure at 'out = text' between ::socket() and the manual close_sock() in own_address_toward leaks the descriptor
policy_floor: manual resource cleanup in NEW C++ not RAII-wrapped
classification_rationale: a new manual close contradicts the RAII-owner rule of the C++ conventions; a fitting owner (yuzu::shared::SocketGuard) was already in the translation unit, so the documented-impossibility exception was refused
summary: New raw ::socket() closed by hand in the live harness leaked a descriptor when an allocation threw (verified with injected out-of-memory: fds 5 to 6); fixed in a638d28c27 by holding the socket in yuzu::shared::SocketGuard, the policy floor met by the letter with a derived band of LOW; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: the Gate 1 Resource Ledger is read against the code: it has no row for StagingDir (a 0700 directory plus a yuzu::TempFile in a shared_ptr) or for FlakyLoadRunner::fn() (a callback context holding this) and says atomic<int> where the code has atomic<unsigned>
policy_floor: Resource Ledger omission on a C++ diff
classification_rationale: required ledger rows are missing and one row misstates a type; no code is wrong
summary: The Gate 1 Resource Ledger omitted two test-only owners and misstated a counter type; fixed by the committed Resource Ledger in this change's governance.d (written from the final code, recorder a person), which adds both owners and corrects the counter to atomic<unsigned>; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: an operator follows the privilege model or the instructions-tests.sh header and runs the wrapper with only --target-agent-hostname, which exits 2 without --console-access-to-agent
classification_rationale: both sentences contradict the wrapper, which requires the second flag
summary: Two sentences said the remote ceremony runs with --target-agent-hostname alone, but the wrapper also requires --console-access-to-agent (exit 2 without it); fixed in a638d28c27 in both places; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

adjudication_rationale: E7 adjudicated to hold: the ceremony is a hand-run lab tool that gates nothing and the URL and password are typed by the operator, so the derived band is MEDIUM and the finding does not block; the guardian had asked for this adjudication. The fix is a warning rather than a refusal because the remote guards were fixed at intake as 'remote flag required for a non-loopback dashboard', the lab dashboards are plain http, and a refusal with no override would stop the remote ceremony from any third host; this touches a guard the owner specified, so a refusal is a two-line change if wanted. The adjudicator is a subagent of the authoring session, so independence is asserted, not enforced.
trigger: an operator runs the remote ceremony against a non-loopback http:// dashboard, so the admin password and session cookie cross the network in cleartext (Client(base) checks no scheme)
classification_rationale: the remote mode lacks any scheme check before the login
summary: The remote ceremony accepted any dashboard URL and logged in over http to a non-loopback host in cleartext; fixed in a638d28c27 with a stderr warning before the login in every mode (host only, never the URL) and the same clause in the help text, a warning rather than a refusal by the Architect's ruling that is flagged for the owner, the warning's order and its Windows-leg skip completed in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-1, G8-29).

trigger: a macOS live run (root or agent account) with the yuzu pf anchor not loaded, which is every clean host at baseline and every host after release, where pfctl answers exit 1 for the absent anchor
classification_rationale: the harness gated the anchor read as [failed] while the plugin's own PfLeg::read_status reads a failed anchor read after two good main reads as 'no anchor', so the harness contradicts the product on a clean host
summary: The macOS live snapshot treated a missing yuzu pf anchor read as failed, which would stop every live case on a clean Mac (verified by running the real comparator; the real pfctl exit status was not observed); fixed in a638d28c27 by the pure predicate pf_anchor_absent (both main reads complete, the anchor call ran to a non-zero exit, no sudo refusal) with unit cases, the comments hedged in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-18), and the real exit and text left to the macOS lab run.

trigger: a macOS root live run compares the plugin's stdout-only pf rule count against the snapshot section that merges stderr and so carries two ALTQ lines
classification_rationale: the two counts are taken over unlike text, so the equality the case asserts cannot hold on a real host
summary: macOS root state and rules counts compared unlike text (the snapshot merges stderr and carries two ALTQ lines the plugin's count does not; verified by running a probe); fixed in a638d28c27 by the pure count_pf_rule_lines that leaves noise lines out, used at both sites, with a fixture.

trigger: an agent that cannot open AF_NETLINK (a unit or seccomp profile denying it) refuses every quarantine permanently with own_addresses_unreadable and no override
classification_rationale: the README, hardening manual, REST reference and alert text give neither the cause nor the remedy of a permanent own_addresses_unreadable refusal
summary: A permanent own_addresses_unreadable refusal where the agent cannot open AF_NETLINK (verified in a container with seccomp denying socket(AF_NETLINK): getifaddrs rc -1, errno 97) was documented with neither cause nor remedy; fixed in a638d28c27 with one sentence each in the README, hardening manual, REST reference and alert description.

trigger: an operator hardens the agent unit with RestrictAddressFamilies= and reads the README for the resulting row
classification_rationale: the README and a header comment attribute RestrictAddressFamilies to the nftables:socket:eperm row, but classify_open_errno files EAFNOSUPPORT as unsupported and keeps it silent
summary: The README and a header comment named systemd RestrictAddressFamilies as the cause of the eperm row although a denied address family answers EAFNOSUPPORT, which is silent; fixed in a638d28c27 as a docs-only correction with no code change; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: an own-address read fails (GetAdaptersAddresses 1228 during a DHCP renew, EMFILE or ENOMEM, or AF_NETLINK denied) and the server retries on backoff for up to 45 minutes while REST and MCP answer success-shaped and the alert names no reason
classification_rationale: no cause, retry signal or audit row surfaces the refusal; the server-side answer shape and the alert carry no reason
summary: A failed own-address read refuses the apply while REST and MCP answer success-shaped and the server retries on backoff for up to 45 minutes; the server-side behaviour is linked to #8424 (an active prioritised issue, evidence added in a comment), while the agent logs the errno and the docs name the cause (a638d28c27).

trigger: a host that holds one of several addresses its server name resolves to (a gateway or replica host) runs the agent, whose control set is resolved at start and never refreshed
classification_rationale: the any-one-match refusal is the planned and pinned design; what is absent is a refresh of the resolved set and an override
summary: A host holding one of the addresses its server name resolves to is never contained, and the resolved set is refreshed only at agent start; the any-one-match rule is the planned, already pinned design, the limit is disclosed in a638d28c27, and the remainder is filed as #8507.

trigger: a VIP, failover or VPN gives the host the server's address between the self-host check and the apply (about 70 s) and the server apply carries no time limit
classification_rationale: server-driven applies send only the exceptions: no ttl and no post-apply re-check; the disclosure is written, the mechanism is absent
summary: An address change between the self-host check and the apply can leave a host contained with console-only recovery because server applies carry no time limit (native high, derived MEDIUM); the disclosure and the stop-the-agent-first step are in a638d28c27 and the server-side time limit and re-check are filed as #8508.

trigger: a ruleset of 100k rules or a churning one, or an agent-account loop on the snapshot word, makes the root helper burn CPU and hold the xtables lock because its 1 MiB cut bounds bytes, not work or time
classification_rationale: the helper snapshot has a byte cap but no timeout, no -w and no accounting
summary: The yuzu-fw-helper snapshot word bounds bytes but not time or work, so a very large or churning ruleset can hold root CPU and the xtables lock; it has no production caller (harness only) and needs a measured bound and a mechanism the root helper lacks, so it is filed as #8509 (a hardening item, no advisory).

trigger: the ceremony script runs on the agent's own machine under another name (a WSL2 lane beside a Windows agent, a container hostname, a VM alias), so the typed-host binding passes while the script host can be cut off
classification_rationale: the remote binding compares only platform.node() and socket.gethostname(); no further check exists
summary: The ceremony's remote binding passes when the script runs on the agent's own machine under another name, so the script host may be cut off and the release left to the time limit; E7 holds (hand-run lab tool, operator-typed input) and the binding is the owner's chosen design, so the remainder, with those of C-37 and C-42, is filed as #8510.

trigger: an evaluator or dev follower runs scripts/whats-new.py with the agent and server on one machine: it prints no Breaking line and cuts bullet 1 at 200 characters
classification_rationale: the breaking change lacks the **Breaking marker that whats-new keys on; not HIGH because the body, the hardening and REST manuals and the README state the consequence
summary: The breaking change was not surfaced as Breaking by scripts/whats-new.py (verified by running it); fixed in a638d28c27 by leading bullet 1 of the changed fragment with a **Breaking marker and adding the issue numbers to bullet 3.

trigger: a device refuses a containment apply with self_host or own_addresses_unreadable: the server writes quarantine.enable and a quarantine.reapply success per dispatch but no failure row
classification_rationale: the required audit site for a refused apply is absent; the refusal words survive only in the response store and the agent warn line
summary: A device's refusal of a containment apply leaves no audit row on the server (the agent side was verified by running a probe, the server writes read from the code); the three sentences claiming nothing is written were corrected in a638d28c27 and the server audit site is linked to #8424 (an active prioritised issue, evidence added in a comment).

trigger: the own-address enumeration is replaced with nullopt or {}, or self_host is added to do_release or do_quarantine_allow: no unit case fails, because the own-address branch is seen only by a hidden live case
classification_rationale: no test pins the wiring of the self-host check (four mutants survived the real agent suite)
summary: Nothing in CI pinned the wiring of the self-host check (four mutants survived the real agent suite, verified by mutation); fixed in a638d28c27 with two small boundary closures that kill all four, and the dispatches made unable to reach the OS completed in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-6, G8-7); the SHOULD label is kept above the INFO the facts derive; exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: deleting IFS, set -f or LC_ALL from the helper leaves test_the_environment_cannot_change_what_runs green: only the PATH= line is observed
classification_rationale: the test name claims an environment guarantee the test cannot observe (10 of 13 in-memory helper mutants die)
summary: test_the_environment_cannot_change_what_runs could not observe what it asserts (three helper mutants survive); fixed in a638d28c27 by renaming both copies to a hostile-PATH test with PATH only and deleting the glob case, the PATH proof strengthened with a planted tool in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-28); no helper change, the SHOULD label kept above the INFO the facts derive; exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: firewall.dll is absent or unloadable when the Windows state and rules cases run: each takes the WARN, SUCCEED, return path and goes green
classification_rationale: the cases lack the build-tree FAIL the live file has, so they pass without running
summary: The new Windows state and rules cases went green when the plugin was absent or unloadable (Windows read, not compiled); fixed in a638d28c27 with a file-local skip_without_plugin that fails under MESON_BUILD_ROOT and skips on a bare run, its comment corrected in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-29), the SHOULD label kept above the INFO the facts derive; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: the Linux nftables probe shell (run_nft_probe, dump_once, the re-run, a table failure on pass two) and the cleanup defects cs-A, cs-B and cs-C are exercised by no unit or sanitizer leg
classification_rationale: no test runs the Linux probe shell; the pure decisions and own_addresses_unreadable are covered
summary: No test runs the Linux nftables probe shell, so no sanitizer leg covers it (the two cleanup defects it named are fixed in a638d28c27); the durable fix is a Linux local-dispatcher case that needs the same placement decision as #8452, so it is filed as #8511.

trigger: uniq.emplace(text_buf) throws bad_alloc between getifaddrs() and the manual freeifaddrs(head), leaking the interface list
classification_rationale: manual cleanup that can leak on a throw contradicts the RAII-owner convention; the pair is byte-identical in enumerate_local_ips() at the merge base
summary: Manual freeifaddrs could leak the interface list when an insertion threw (verified with counting shims; the pair predates the branch, so SHOULD rather than the policy floor, native SHOULD, derived LOW); fixed in a638d28c27 with std::unique_ptr<ifaddrs, decltype(&freeifaddrs)>, then re-verified in round 2 by allocation-failure injection at every allocation point; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: the own-address read runs eagerly as a call argument, so a loopback control still triggers the OS read, and a bad_alloc there turns self_host into degraded|exception
classification_rationale: the header says a loopback or unspecified control is refused 'without consulting the enumeration', which is false at the call site
summary: The call-site comment claimed the enumeration is not consulted for a loopback control although the read runs eagerly and a throw there maps to degraded|exception; fixed in a638d28c27 as a comment only (no callable, no throw wrapper) because self_host_refusal already takes the read's value and a throw anywhere in the seam gives the same documented answer (native SHOULD, derived LOW); impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: a future copy of a KeptStream closes one descriptor twice, or a second open() orphans the first socket; no site does either today
classification_rationale: resource owners must be non-copyable per the C++ conventions; KeptStream had implicit copy operations
summary: KeptStream had implicit copy operations (a copy would close one descriptor twice) although no site copies it (pre-existing, derived LOW, the floor not met); fixed in a638d28c27 by deleting copy construction and assignment, with no SocketGuard member and no reopen guard because both uses are fresh locals; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: an operator reads that only an operator's quarantine is checked, but a REST record's first apply is the reconciler's and every server apply and MCP re-apply sends a plain firewall.quarantine, so they are checked and a transient getifaddrs failure refuses them
classification_rationale: the documented scope of the check contradicts do_quarantine, which checks every non-repair dispatch; the wire has no caller field
summary: The docs and the change summary said only an operator's quarantine is checked, which is false (every firewall.quarantine apply is checked whoever sent it); fixed in a638d28c27 by accepting the code and rewriting the sentences with the exemptions (an active own record, repair, boot re-apply, release, quarantine_allow), the wording completed in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-15, G8-16, G8-19); impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: an operator on the packaged Linux unit (or behind a non-own server address) follows 'the one case that is not refused' and 'a plain DELETE ends the record'
classification_rationale: do_release opens with privilege_refusal(), so a plain DELETE stays releasing on the packaged unit and needs ?force=true; the first sentence omits that a server behind a non-own address also passes
summary: Two sentences overstated: a server behind a non-own address also passes, and a plain DELETE does not end a record on the packaged Linux unit, where release is refused first and ?force=true is needed; both reworded in a638d28c27; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: a completed pfctl -s info (exit 0) has neither Status: Enabled nor Disabled, or a completed socketfilterfw read is garbled: pf|unknown or state|unknown appears with no error row
classification_rationale: the 'if and only if' claim is false when the read completed but was not recognised
summary: The claim that pf|unknown appears if and only if the pf info error row does was false for a completed but unrecognised read (verified by running it); fixed in a638d28c27 in the README, the macOS banner, the YAML and the changelog bullet, with the in-code test comment scoped in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-17).

trigger: an operator follows 'end it with DELETE, and with ?force=true when that answers 202' and repeats the DELETE
classification_rationale: the sentence contradicts the DELETE section (poll, do not repeat the DELETE; force only if still releasing)
summary: A REST-manual sentence said to end a record with DELETE and with ?force=true when that answers 202, contradicting the DELETE section (poll, do not repeat the DELETE; force only while still releasing); aligned in a638d28c27; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: the control endpoint is a container bridge address (for example 172.17.0.2:50051): it is not refused, the table has forward at policy drop with no rules, and the server's published ports vanish for the whole fleet
classification_rationale: the bridge-address limit is disclosed but its consequence (forward drop, no time limit on server applies, the repair undoing a removal, the exits) is not
summary: The bridge-address limit was disclosed but not its consequence (forwarded traffic dropped, no time limit on server applies, the exits); fixed in a638d28c27 with one passage in the hardening manual, REST reference and README, its console-recovery steps made followable in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-11, G8-12); native SHOULD-FIX, derived LOW; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: a server in a container at a bridge IP on the agent's host: the check is address-only, so the host is contained (TTL 900 s) although the docs say an agent and server on one host always end refused|self_host
classification_rationale: the categorical claim contradicts the address-only check
summary: Docs and ceremony texts said an agent and server on one host always end refused|self_host, but the check is address-only; fixed in a638d28c27 in the skill, the wrapper and the ceremony texts, the --help epilog survivor completed in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-20).

trigger: an operator reads the documented dump labels while the code writes error|nftables:generation:changed and error|nftables:generation:torn_persistent
classification_rationale: the documented label list names table, chain and rule only; the generation label is emitted by the code
summary: The code emits error|nftables:generation:changed and :torn_persistent but the docs listed only table, chain and rule labels; fixed in a638d28c27 in the README and firewall.yaml with the README fences and firewall.json regenerated.

trigger: install-agent-user.sh --dry-run where /etc/sudoers.d/yuzu-agent exists and the helper directory is refused
classification_rationale: the dry run reports a failure that cannot happen (a real run says the file was removed) because remove_sudoers only prints
summary: In --dry-run with the sudoers file present and the helper directory refused, the installer reported a removal failure that cannot happen; fixed in a638d28c27 by testing DRY_RUN before the -e, with a test that fails on the previous installer, the dry-run failure text completed in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-26); impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: install-agent-user.sh --dry-run where the helper directory path is a dangling symlink or a non-directory: the dry run exits 0 while the real run exits 1
classification_rationale: the changelog promise that a dry run exits as the real run would has this exception
summary: A dry run exited 0 where the real run exits 1 for a dangling link or non-directory at the helper directory path (verified: dry rc 0, real rc 1); fixed in a638d28c27 by refusing in the dry run too, with subtests that fail on the previous installer; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: a non-root live run on a host where classic sudo prints 'unable to resolve host': merge_stderr=true puts that warning ahead of the first section header
classification_rationale: the baseline stops with 'text ahead of the first section' although the snapshot itself is sound (loud, never a false pass)
summary: Merging stderr into the helper snapshot let sudo's unable-to-resolve-host warning precede the first header, stopping every non-root baseline; fixed in a638d28c27 with merge_stderr=false at both sites (the helper already drops tool stderr and a sudo refusal still fails closed), the stray-text guard pinned under C-65.

trigger: an address that is not on an interface (a cloud elastic or floating IP, a port forward, a Linux local route), another netns, or a name resolving to several addresses is met by the self-host guard
classification_rationale: the header's 'still skipped' holds on Windows only (POSIX has no IFF_UP test) and the hardening limit names bridge addresses only
summary: The self-host guard cannot see NAT, floating or port-forwarded addresses or other namespaces, and the header comment claimed a not-up skip that holds on Windows only; fixed in a638d28c27 by extending the known-limit bullet and correcting the comment.

trigger: standing refused records keep YuzuQuarantineEndpointUnconfirmed (reachability=connected, for 15m, no device label) firing, so a later genuine failure gives no new notification and the reason is only in the agent log; about 32 audit rows a day
classification_rationale: the alert carries no reason and no per-device label; the expression and labels are server-side
summary: Standing refused records pin the unconfirmed-endpoint alert and hide the reason; the alert expression and labels are server-side, so it is linked to #8424 with C-10 (an active prioritised issue, the pinned-alert point added to its evidence comment), and the description text was fixed under C-39 in a638d28c27.

trigger: a snapshot tool exits non-zero or is cut (no ip6_tables, nft without nf_tables, a held xtables lock, an nft section over 1 MiB): the whole snapshot is unreadable and the live harness fails
classification_rationale: the reporter asks for a tolerance the harness deliberately lacks; no text contradicts the behaviour
summary: Any non-zero snapshot tool or a cut makes the whole snapshot unreadable and the live case fails loudly; rejected as by design (the owner's intake decision is that an empty or unreadable snapshot fails the case) and already pinned by SnapshotRuns cases, the held-xtables-lock case being in the issue filed for C-13 (#8509).

trigger: status reads end after about 10 s unchanged and the ceremony never reads server records (a false exit 3 RELEASE NOT CONFIRMED); flock ENOLCK reads as 'held'; O_TRUNC precedes the write (an empty --record JSON)
classification_rationale: ceremony messages and exit statuses state more than the script established
summary: Ceremony honesty gaps: a failed --record could destroy an earlier record, flock ENOLCK read as another run holding the lock, and slow status reads ended as RELEASE NOT CONFIRMED; the first two are fixed in a638d28c27 (a record is never overwritten via C-42; any OSError other than BlockingIOError is its own lock_failed reason, exit 2, nothing dispatched) with tests, and the remainder is carried by #8510.

trigger: an unprivileged macOS agent runs state: a permanent pf|unknown plus three error|pf:*:exit:1 rows, and load timeouts flap state|unknown
classification_rationale: the reporter asks for fewer rows; the rows are the designed disclosure and no text contradicts the code
summary: An unprivileged macOS agent answers unknown plus up to three error rows that say why; rejected as a designed outcome (the behaviour the open macOS issues ask for, stated in the changelog), with the load-timeout observation kept on the macOS lab checklist (C-75).

trigger: an operator reads the YuzuQuarantineEndpointUnconfirmed description: it gives a false cause for own_addresses_unreadable (offering DELETE instead of fixing the read), omits that a plain DELETE resolves the alert within a tick while a refused release stays stuck, and points to neither the reason nor the device
classification_rationale: the alert description contradicts the code on the cause of unreadable and omits where the token is read
summary: The alert description gave a false cause for own_addresses_unreadable and omitted where the token is read and the DELETE and ?force=true exits (native SHOULD-FIX, the reporter disagreeing with its own label: derived LOW); fixed in a638d28c27 as description text only (expression, for and labels untouched, the YAML parses), with the recovery wording single-sourced in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-11, G8-19).

trigger: getifaddrs fails (AF_NETLINK denied, errno 97, or a transient EMFILE): the errno is dropped and nothing logs it
classification_rationale: the failure cause is absent from every log and return value, so permanent and transient failures look the same
summary: The errno or return code of a failed own-address read was dropped, so a permanent failure could not be told from a transient one without strace; fixed in a638d28c27 with one spdlog::warn in each collect() arm (errno captured immediately, no return-type change, no once-flag), the cadence on a persistent failure reviewed and accepted in round 2 (G8-23).

trigger: one standing refused record on an otherwise idle single-host server: each refusal counts as yuzu_commands_completed_total{status=error} and YuzuHighCommandFailureRate can fire repeatedly
classification_rationale: the self-host paragraph does not say the alert can flap with the record or where the refusal is visible
summary: Each refused apply counts as a failed command, so YuzuHighCommandFailureRate can fire on an otherwise idle server while a refused record stands (modelled by the reporter, not run); fixed in a638d28c27 with one hedged sentence and the places to see the refusal.

trigger: a second ceremony run at the same --record path replaces the first record (O_TRUNC), so a refused rerun erases a pass; the record also lacks operator, dashboard, command ids and end time
classification_rationale: the retained record is thin and overwritable; evidence fields are absent
summary: The --record file was a weak retained record that a second run overwrote (O_TRUNC, so a refused rerun erased a pass); fixed in a638d28c27 by opening it O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL so a record is never overwritten (which also closes C-37(c) and C-49), its two follow-on defects (a guard hiding a failed write, a partial file blocking the retry) fixed in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-2, G8-4), and the extra record fields carried by #8510.

trigger: an operator on the packaged Linux unit reads that a contained device can always be released, but do_release opens with privilege_refusal()
classification_rationale: 'can always be released' contradicts do_release's privilege refusal on the packaged Linux unit
summary: 'Can always be released' was false on the packaged Linux unit, where release is refused first and only a forced end works; reworded in a638d28c27 in the README and the hardening manual.

trigger: the kContainmentUi flag flips, or the fragment URL is opened, for a refused device: the lens says 'Applied to the device but not yet confirmed' and its confirm dialog has no self-host caveat
classification_rationale: the lens label contradicts the device's refusal because the server stamps last_applied_at on dispatch acceptance
summary: The dashboard containment lens mislabels a refused device as applied but unconfirmed and its confirm dialog lacks the self-host caveat (pre-existing, latent behind kContainmentUi=false, outside this agent-side change); filed as #8512.

trigger: an operator reads that a torn dump gets exactly one more look: a torn TABLE dump gets no re-read, and the re-run needs 2 s of the budget left
classification_rationale: the README says a torn or moved-generation dump gets one more look; run_nft_probe returns at a failed table dump and the re-run needs kNftRerunFloor
summary: The README and the privilege model said a torn dump always gets one more look, but a failed table dump gets no re-read and a re-run needs at least 2 s of the budget; fixed in a638d28c27 in the README and the privilege model, the YAML survivor and its generated mirrors completed in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-21); impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: an operator reads appfirewall:<globalstate|listapps> as state tokens, but only appfirewall:globalstate is emitted for state
classification_rationale: the state description names a token the state action never emits
summary: The state description named appfirewall:listapps although only globalstate is emitted for state; fixed in a638d28c27 in firewall.yaml with the README fence and firewall.json regenerated; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: an operator reads that a # comment line never causes the unrecognised-output row, but ufw_shape_ok is false for a # note line before the header, after it and after Status: inactive
classification_rationale: the claim holds for iptables -S only, where iptables_shape_ok skips # lines
summary: The README said a # comment line never triggers the unrecognised row, which holds for iptables -S only; fixed in a638d28c27 to say iptables only; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: a reader meets stale counts and omissions ('one of two kinds of call ... A third call', 'Two limits', diagrams without the new error rows and the generation check, a refused list without the two tokens) and a private roadmap id in public test text
classification_rationale: wording and count drift in prose the diff touches; docs-writer owns wording
summary: Stale counts, diagram omissions and a private roadmap id in public text (README, privilege model, test comments and meson.build); all updated in a638d28c27 in one docs pass, the private id replaced by an issue number and a stale test-count comment corrected; impact and exposure derived by the recorder.

trigger: --record on a non-POSIX interpreter (Python up to 3.12 on Windows): refusal() stops the run, but main()'s finally still reaches os.fchmod and raises AttributeError in place of exit 2, leaving a 0-byte record
classification_rationale: the script promises exit 2 and a record on every exit path; a POSIX-only call breaks that off POSIX
summary: On a non-POSIX interpreter --record raised AttributeError in place of exit 2 and left a 0-byte record (verified by emulation); closed in a638d28c27 by the C-42 edit (no POSIX-only call is left in write_record) with a test, the test made able to fail in 3d0ef78f4c (G8-27).
